system_requirements.name: Verified production identity and tenant context
system_requirements.requirement: Every command must receive a server-verified actor_id, tenant_id, tenant membership, and action permission from the approved identity provider. Public requester access must use a scoped verified request capability and must not expose staff permissions.
system_requirements.secret_policy: Keep provider credentials server-side and outside product records. Persist only non-secret provider subject references when policy permits.

when: request capability is expired or mismatched
fail_closed.result: reject before reading sensitive records or writing state

system_requirements.name: Durable tenant-scoped transactional persistence
system_requirements.requirement: Persist canonical records, optimistic revisions, idempotency results, audit entries, and outbox events in a durable database with tenant_id on every key and restrictive foreign keys.
system_requirements.secret_policy: Do not persist database credentials or raw connection secrets in architecture or business records.

fail_closed.result: roll back the full command and emit no success response

system_requirements.name: Atomic command idempotency ledger
system_requirements.requirement: Reserve tenant_id, command_id, and idempotency_key atomically with a request digest, then retain the recorded result and event_id for safe retries.
system_requirements.secret_policy: Store request digests and non-secret correlation values, not raw tokens or provider secrets.

when: the same key has a different request digest
fail_closed.result: reject mutation or return the exact recorded result; never execute twice

system_requirements.name: Transactional audit and event delivery
system_requirements.requirement: Write each domain event with tenant_id, event_id, command_id, idempotency_key, actor_id, entity refs, prior state, next state, policy refs, and occurred_at in the same transaction as state. Deliver from an at-least-once outbox with consumer idempotency.
system_requirements.secret_policy: Events may carry stable refs and approved audit facts but no raw secrets or unrestricted evidence payloads.

when: the event cannot be written atomically
a required entity or state reference is absent

system_requirements.name: Authorized evidence object storage
system_requirements.requirement: Store evidence objects outside canonical JSON records through immutable object refs, tenant-scoped authorization, integrity hashes, content scanning, and short-lived access grants. The request_evidence entity retains metadata and version lineage.
system_requirements.secret_policy: Never persist raw storage credentials or long-lived signed URLs. Keep restricted evidence out of events and notification bodies.

fail_closed.result: reject the evidence command and do not mark evidence usable

system_requirements.name: Versioned operating rules and SLA targets
system_requirements.requirement: Resolve qualification, assignment, evidence, readiness, escalation, retention, and service-level targets from an owner-manager-approved policy version. Record the applied policy ref and any computed target_at with each decision. This architecture defines no default response-time promise.
system_requirements.secret_policy: Policies contain rules and references only, not identity-provider, notification-provider, or database secrets.

when: a required policy version is missing
an SLA target cannot be derived for an action that requires one
fail_closed.result: block the transition and open or update an attributable authority exception

system_requirements.name: Approved post-commit notifications
system_requirements.requirement: Send only policy-permitted requester, assignee, escalation, and recipient notices after commit through an approved channel. Retain delivery attempts without treating delivery as a workflow decision.
system_requirements.secret_policy: Keep channel credentials server-side. Notification payloads must exclude staff-only risk notes, unrestricted evidence, and raw secrets.

when: recipient consent or authority is absent
channel classification does not permit the payload

customer_copy.primary_state: The current package keeps its readiness decision, evidence, limits, recipient access, and open obligations together.
customer_copy.empty_state: No handoff package exists. A current quote-ready decision and verified recipient are required first.
customer_copy.error_state: The package was not transferred. Review the named recipient, access, evidence, or version problem.

signature_interactions.name: Follow the request spine
signature_interactions.description: Opening any queue item anchors the source request in the center while assignment, evidence, field facts, readiness, and handoff attach around it. Switching work modes never replaces the active request with a generic dashboard.

signature_interactions.name: Stitch evidence to a decision
signature_interactions.description: Selecting a readiness criterion reveals only the exact current evidence versions that support it. A result cannot be recorded until the reviewer addresses missing, disputed, restricted, or stale evidence.

signature_interactions.name: One guarded next move
signature_interactions.description: The bottom dock presents one command allowed by current state, permission, policy, and revision. It explains blocked guards in customer language and sends authority questions to the named human role.

signature_interactions.name: Seal and receive the handoff
signature_interactions.description: The handoff compacts the current readiness decision, evidence refs, limitations, recipient access, and open obligations into an immutable receipt. Later changes visibly invalidate the seal without erasing transfer or acknowledgement history.

visual_language.color_system: Use warm paper and graphite neutrals for the dossier, oxidized copper for the active stitch and focus ring, field blue for links and neutral progress, amber for unresolved checks, and brick red for stopped work. Every color has a text label and icon. Meet WCAG AA contrast in all states and never use color alone to signal readiness.
visual_language.data_visualization: Use a thin chronological stitch for attributable events, compact checklist rows for evidence coverage, and queue aging as labeled elapsed time. Do not add charts without retained source data, a decision they support, and an accessible table equivalent.
visual_language.shape_language: A strong vertical spine, offset clipped rails, narrow stitched connectors, square evidence thumbnails, and a rounded bottom command dock. Use borders and spacing to show attachment and version lineage. Avoid a uniform field of floating rounded cards.
visual_language.typography: Use a sturdy humanist sans for instructions and controls, tabular numerals for times and versions, and a restrained slab or serif accent only for request identifiers and section folios. Preserve 16px body text, 1.5 line height, visible focus, 44px touch targets, and readable layout at 200 percent zoom.

sops.name: Record and qualify an estimate request
sops.trigger: A service requester contacts the company through an approved public or staff-assisted channel to request an estimate.
preconditions: The intake channel can identify its source and record the requester's consent for follow-up.
The office coordinator can apply the owner-manager's current service-area, work-type, and risk rules.
inputs: Requester name and usable contact details
Available photos, measurements, access notes, and other request evidence

steps.action: Create one intake record and preserve the source channel, received time, requester details, service location, requested work, and follow-up consent.
Check the request against the current minimum-information, supported-work, service-area, and risk rules without treating the request as accepted work.
Record the attributable qualification result as supported, clarification required, owner review required, or declined, together with the reason and next action.

outputs: One traceable intake record
An attributable qualification result and reason
A named next action or accountable owner
A requester follow-up record when information is missing
controls: Only authorized staff may qualify, decline, or route a request.
The original channel source and received details remain in the audit history after correction.
Qualification cannot mark the package quote-ready or replace accounting or dispatch records.
Requester contact and location data follow tenant access and retention policy.
metrics: Qualified estimate requests created
Qualified estimate-request completion rate
Share of submitted requests containing required contact, location, and work details
Median time from request capture to first human response
Median age of requests awaiting clarification or owner review

exception_paths.condition: Required contact, location, work, consent, or access information is missing or contradictory.
exception_paths.action: Set clarification required, identify the missing fields, contact the requester, and retain each attempt and response.

exception_paths.condition: The work appears outside current service, area, access, or risk rules.
exception_paths.action: Prevent automatic acceptance and route the request with its evidence to the owner-manager for a recorded decision.

exception_paths.condition: The same request arrives through more than one channel.
exception_paths.action: Link the records for human review, preserve each source, and avoid silently discarding or merging requester information.

sops.name: Prioritize and assign a qualified request
sops.trigger: An estimate request has an attributable supported qualification result and is ready for accountable estimator assignment.
preconditions: The request has the minimum requester, location, requested-work, consent, and qualification information.
Current estimator eligibility, service-area, work-type, workload, and escalation rules are available.
inputs: Work type and known access or risk notes
priority_rules: Apply only owner-manager-approved service, risk, timing, and capacity rules.
Do not infer priority from customer value, revenue, or unconnected sales records.
Record the rule and facts used for any priority change.
owner_rules: Assign only an estimator eligible for the request's work type, service area, access needs, and known risk.
Every accepted request has one accountable coordinator until the estimator acknowledges the handoff.
The owner-manager resolves eligibility conflicts, capacity exceptions, and reassignment disputes.
sops.service_level: Use the current owner-manager policy for response, assignment, and acknowledgement targets. Record the applicable target with the request instead of inventing a default commitment.
sops.escalation: Route unassignable, overdue, disputed, capacity-constrained, or risk-flagged requests to the owner-manager with the blocking reason, current owner, and requested decision.
sops.audit_event: Record priority calculation, assignment, acknowledgement, rejection, reassignment, and escalation with actor, time, policy or reason, and affected request.

steps.action: Apply the current priority rules to the qualified request and record the facts and policy used.
Select an eligible estimator under the current assignment rules and send the complete request package for acknowledgement.
Record the estimator's acknowledgement or return reason and keep an accountable owner for the next action.

outputs: A policy-backed priority record
An accountable estimator assignment or an owner-manager escalation
An acknowledgement, return reason, or reassignment record
A visible next action and applicable target
controls: Only authorized coordinators or owner-managers may assign or reassign estimators.
Assignment never overrides estimator eligibility, access, or risk restrictions.
Every priority and ownership change retains actor, time, reason, and prior value.
A returned assignment cannot leave the request without an accountable coordinator.
metrics: Share of accepted requests with an accountable coordinator and estimator
Share of site visits assigned to an accountable estimator
Median time from qualification to estimator acknowledgement
Count and median age of requests awaiting assignment or reassignment

exception_paths.condition: No eligible estimator is available under current service, capacity, access, or risk rules.
exception_paths.action: Keep the coordinator accountable and escalate the constraint and requested decision to the owner-manager.

exception_paths.condition: The estimator returns the assignment because intake information is incomplete.
exception_paths.action: Record the reason, return the request to clarification without losing assignment history, and tell the requester what is needed.

exception_paths.condition: The request passes its recorded assignment or acknowledgement target.
exception_paths.action: Escalate the overdue request with its age, current owner, and next action under the current policy.

sops.name: Control request and site evidence
sops.trigger: A requester, coordinator, or estimator supplies a photo, measurement, access note, scope note, or other evidence used in qualification or quote-readiness decisions.
preconditions: The evidence can be linked to one service request and an attributable source.
The submitting actor has permission to add or view the evidence classification.
inputs: Evidence type, source, and visibility classification
Correction or supersession reason when replacing prior evidence
classification: Classify evidence by type, source, requester visibility, sensitivity, and the decision it may support.
Keep requester-visible evidence separate from staff-only risk, access, or decision notes.
sops.versioning: Create a new version for a correction, replacement, annotation, or changed measurement. Preserve the prior version, source, author, time, and supersession reason.
sops.review: The accountable estimator reviews evidence needed for quote-readiness. The office coordinator reviews intake completeness, and the owner-manager reviews evidence attached to escalated decisions.
sops.retention: Apply the approved tenant retention policy by evidence classification and request state. Do not silently delete evidence used in an attributable decision.
sops.access_control: Limit requester evidence, contact data, locations, access notes, and staff-only risk notes to authorized tenant roles and requester-visible views defined by policy.
sops.audit_event: Record evidence creation, classification, version, review, access-policy change, supersession, and retention action with actor, time, request, and reason.

steps.action: Link the evidence to the request and record its source, capture time, evidence type, visibility, sensitivity, and submitting actor.
Create a retained version when evidence is corrected, annotated, or replaced and record why the prior version was superseded.
Review the required evidence for completeness, usability, requester visibility, and decision relevance, then record the result and missing items.

outputs: Versioned evidence linked to one request and source
An attributable evidence review result
A list of missing, unusable, disputed, or restricted items
An audit trail for classification and supersession
controls: Evidence used in a decision retains its source, actor, time, version, and classification.
Prior evidence versions remain available under the retention policy after correction.
Requester-visible and staff-only evidence obey separate access rules.
Secrets and unrelated personal data cannot be stored as request evidence.
metrics: Share of quote-ready decisions with required photos, measurements, scope notes, and accountable estimator
Share of accepted requests missing required site evidence at estimator handoff
Count of evidence items returned for missing source, unusable content, or wrong classification
Median time from evidence request to reviewed evidence

exception_paths.condition: Evidence is unreadable, incomplete, unlinked, or missing an attributable source.
exception_paths.action: Mark the item unusable for the decision, preserve it under policy, and request a corrected item with the reason.

exception_paths.condition: The requester disputes a photo, measurement, access note, or scope note.
exception_paths.action: Preserve both versions and the dispute, stop dependent approval if material, and assign a human review.

exception_paths.condition: Evidence appears to contain a secret, unrelated personal data, or an unauthorized staff-only note.
exception_paths.action: Restrict access, prevent decision use, and route the item to the owner-manager for policy-compliant remediation without copying the sensitive content.

sops.name: Resolve an intake or estimating exception
sops.trigger: A request cannot proceed under normal intake, assignment, access, evidence, capacity, service, or risk rules.
preconditions: The blocked request, current state, accountable owner, and blocking reason are known.
The exception can be classified without changing the source request or prior decision history.
inputs: Relevant request, assignment, evidence, and contact history
exception_types: Site access, safety, privacy, or evidence problem
Overdue acknowledgement, clarification, review, or handoff
sops.owner: The office coordinator owns intake clarification, the estimator owns site-evidence correction, and the owner-manager owns policy, risk, capacity, and overdue escalations.
sops.target_date: Set a target from the current exception and service policy. Record the policy basis, and require owner-manager review when no approved target applies.
sops.escalation: Escalate an overdue, disputed, policy-ambiguous, safety-related, privacy-related, or ownerless exception to the owner-manager with the current facts and requested decision.
sops.resolution_evidence: Retain the decision, deciding actor, time, policy or rationale, supporting evidence refs, requester communication when applicable, and the next state or action.
sops.audit_event: Record exception creation, classification, assignment, target change, escalation, resolution, reopening, and closure with actor, time, prior value, and reason.

steps.action: Classify the exception, record its blocking facts, current state, accountable owner, requested decision, and policy-backed target.
Assign and complete the resolution action without erasing the source request, prior decision, evidence, or assignment history.
Record the attributable resolution and evidence, notify affected actors, and reopen the request only at the permitted next state.

outputs: A classified exception with owner and target date
An attributable resolution or documented decline
Resolution evidence and affected-actor notification
A permitted next state, next action, or retained closure reason
controls: An exception cannot silently override service, risk, access, privacy, or permission rules.
Only the documented authority may approve a policy exception.
Changing a target or owner retains the prior value and reason.
Closure requires resolution evidence or a documented decision not to proceed.
metrics: Count and median age of unresolved intake and estimator exceptions
Share of exceptions with an accountable owner and target date
Share of resolved exceptions with attributable resolution evidence
Count of reopened exceptions by type

exception_paths.condition: The exception has no eligible owner or the policy does not identify decision authority.
exception_paths.action: Prevent an automatic decision and route the authority gap to the owner-manager for a recorded policy decision.

exception_paths.condition: The target date passes without a resolution record.
exception_paths.action: Escalate the exception with its age, current owner, attempts, and requested decision; retain the original target.

exception_paths.condition: New facts materially contradict the recorded resolution.
exception_paths.action: Reopen the exception as a new review event, link the prior resolution, and preserve both decisions.

sops.name: Review and decide quote readiness
sops.trigger: The assigned estimator believes the request package has enough current evidence to make a quote-ready decision.
preconditions: The estimator has acknowledged the assignment and can view the qualification record and retained evidence.
Any required site visit is documented or an attributable decision states why it is not required.
Material exceptions are resolved or remain listed as blockers.
inputs: Required photos, measurements, access notes, and scope notes
Known exclusions, assumptions, unresolved questions, and exception decisions
entry_criteria: The request has an accountable estimator.
The required intake and site evidence is present, current, attributable, and reviewed.
Scope notes identify the requested work, known exclusions, assumptions, and unresolved blockers.
The package does not rely on an unresolved service, safety, access, privacy, or permission exception.
review_checklist: Confirm the request, service location, and requested work match the current requester-visible record.
Confirm required photos, measurements, site observations, and scope notes are usable and versioned.
Confirm exclusions, assumptions, access limits, and unresolved questions are visible.
Confirm the reviewer has authority to record the decision and identify any separate quote-issuing authority.
sops.decision_authority: The assigned estimator records quote-ready or not-ready when authorized by the owner-manager's role policy. The owner-manager resolves policy exceptions but does not erase the estimator's evidence review.
sops.rejection_path: Record not-ready with the failed criterion, correction owner, required evidence or decision, and next review condition. Return the package to the correct prior step without deleting the submitted review.
sops.decision_record: Retain the decision, reviewer, time, criteria version, checklist result, evidence refs, not-ready reasons or limitations, and resulting next action.

steps.action: Check entry criteria and the review checklist against the current retained request, assignment, site, scope, and exception evidence.
Record quote-ready with supporting evidence and limitations, or record not-ready with each failed criterion, correction owner, and required next action.
Notify the coordinator and requester as permitted, and route policy or risk blockers to the owner-manager without issuing a quote automatically.

outputs: An attributable quote-ready or not-ready decision
Checklist results and supporting evidence refs
Recorded limitations, failed criteria, or unresolved blockers
A correction, escalation, or downstream handoff action
controls: Only an authorized estimator records quote readiness.
Quote-ready requires retained evidence and cannot be inferred from assignment or visit completion alone.
A quote-ready decision does not issue, price, approve, or send a quote.
Re-review creates a new attributable decision and preserves prior decisions.
metrics: Quote-ready packages completed
Median time from qualified request to quote-ready decision
Share of assigned requests returned for missing intake information
Share of quote-ready decisions with required evidence and an accountable estimator

exception_paths.condition: A required item is missing, stale, disputed, unusable, or lacks an attributable source.
exception_paths.action: Record not-ready, identify the failed criterion and correction owner, and request the specific evidence or clarification.

exception_paths.condition: A service, safety, access, privacy, or permission issue needs policy authority.
exception_paths.action: Keep the package not-ready and route the blocker and evidence to the owner-manager for a separate recorded decision.

exception_paths.condition: The requester changes the requested work or corrects a material fact during review.
exception_paths.action: Version the corrected information, invalidate affected checklist results, and repeat the applicable qualification or evidence review.

sops.name: Handoff a quote-ready package
sops.trigger: An authorized estimator has recorded an evidence-backed quote-ready decision and identified the permitted downstream recipient.
preconditions: The quote-ready decision resolves to the current request, criteria version, reviewer, and supporting evidence.
The recipient is authorized to receive the package and understands that this product does not automatically issue a quote or replace accounting or dispatch.
Open obligations and requester-visible limitations are identified.
inputs: Qualified request, assignment, site-visit, and evidence package
Scope notes, exclusions, assumptions, and unresolved obligations
completion_criteria: The current quote-ready decision and its evidence are included.
The recipient, handoff time, access scope, and package version are recorded.
Open obligations have named owners and next actions.
The recipient has acknowledged receipt or the acknowledgement remains a visible pending obligation.
sops.handoff_recipient: An authorized staff member or approved external process responsible for preparing or issuing the quote. Recipient identity and authority must be recorded for each handoff.
sops.acknowledgement: Record recipient acknowledgement, rejection, or inability to access the package with actor, time, package version, and reason. Lack of acknowledgement remains open and cannot be treated as quote issuance.
sops.open_obligations: List unresolved requester communication, evidence limitations, access arrangements, pricing inputs, approvals, and external-system work with an owner and next action. Do not mark these complete without attributable evidence.
sops.retention: Retain the handed-off package, decision, acknowledgement, and open-obligation history under the approved tenant policy. Preserve evidence used for the decision and do not infer quote, won-work, revenue, or customer outcomes.

steps.action: Assemble the current quote-ready decision, evidence refs, scope notes, limitations, open obligations, recipient, and package version.
Transfer the package through an approved channel with access limited to the authorized recipient and record the handoff event.
Record acknowledgement, rejection, or access failure and keep every open obligation assigned until separately completed or closed with a reason.

outputs: A versioned handoff package and attributable handoff event
Recipient acknowledgement, rejection, or access-failure record
A retained list of open obligations with owners and next actions
Completion evidence limited to the quote-ready handoff
controls: Only authorized recipients receive requester and site evidence.
The handoff retains the exact package version, decision, actor, time, and method.
Handoff completion does not imply quote issuance, customer acceptance, won work, or revenue.
Open obligations cannot disappear when ownership changes.
metrics: Share of quote-ready packages acknowledged by an authorized recipient
Median time from quote-ready decision to handoff acknowledgement
Count and median age of open handoff obligations
Quotes issued from quote-ready packages only when an attributable quote record is available

exception_paths.condition: The recipient lacks authority or cannot access the package.
exception_paths.action: Stop the transfer, preserve the failed attempt without copying restricted evidence, and assign access correction or a new authorized recipient.

exception_paths.condition: The recipient rejects the package because required evidence or scope information is incomplete.
exception_paths.action: Record the rejection reason, preserve the handoff history, return the package to not-ready review, and assign the correction.

exception_paths.condition: A material request or evidence change occurs after handoff.
exception_paths.action: Version the changed information, notify the recipient, invalidate the affected handoff package, and require a new quote-ready review before re-handoff.

sops.name: Coordinate a site visit and capture the estimate scope
sops.trigger: A qualified request has an acknowledged estimator assignment and the office coordinator or estimator determines that a site visit is required before quote-readiness review.
preconditions: The request has a supported qualification decision and an accountable office coordinator.
An eligible estimator has acknowledged the assignment.
The requester has consented to follow-up, and staff can view the service location and approved access notes.
Current site-evidence requirements and any known access, safety, privacy, or service restrictions are available.
inputs: Qualified service request and current requester-visible details
Requester availability and approved contact channel
Site location, access notes, and known restrictions
Required photo, measurement, observation, and scope-note checklist

steps.action: Record why a site visit is required, the evidence to collect, the assigned estimator, and any access or safety conditions that affect scheduling.
Offer permitted visit windows through the approved contact channel and record when and how the requester received them.
Accept or decline an offered window and provide corrections or access instructions without changing staff-only notes or the estimator assignment.
Confirm the scheduled window, evidence checklist, access conditions, and accountable estimator with the requester through an approved channel.

At the visit, record arrival and completion facts, collect the required photos and measurements, and write scope notes, exclusions, assumptions, access limits, and unresolved questions with attributable sources.

Compare the captured scope with the current requester-visible request, record material differences or missing items, and route the package to quote-readiness review only when the site-visit record is complete.

outputs: A scheduled, completed, cancelled, or no-access site-visit record with accountable actors and times
Versioned site photos, measurements, observations, and scope notes linked to the request
Recorded exclusions, assumptions, access limits, and unresolved questions
A complete package routed to quote-readiness review or a named correction or escalation action
controls: Only an authorized coordinator may confirm the visit window, and only the assigned authorized estimator may complete the field record.
A scheduled or completed visit does not make a request quote-ready; the estimator must perform the separate quote-readiness review.
Requester-visible details and staff-only access, safety, and risk notes follow separate permission rules.
Each schedule change, access outcome, evidence item, scope correction, and completion decision retains its actor, time, prior value, and reason.
The procedure does not issue a quote or change accounting or dispatch records.
metrics: Share of required site visits with a requester-confirmed window and accountable estimator
Median time from estimator acknowledgement to completed site visit
Share of completed site visits containing the required photos, measurements, and scope notes
Count and median age of visits awaiting requester confirmation, access correction, or rescheduling
Share of site-visit packages returned from quote-readiness review for missing or conflicting field evidence

exception_paths.condition: The requester declines every offered window, stops responding, or changes availability after confirmation.
exception_paths.action: Preserve the contact and scheduling history, keep the coordinator accountable, and record a rescheduling action or policy-backed closure reason.

exception_paths.condition: The estimator cannot access the site or encounters an undisclosed safety, privacy, service, or authorization restriction.
exception_paths.action: Stop the affected work, record the access outcome without exposing restricted details, and route the blocker and requested decision to the owner-manager.

exception_paths.condition: Required photos, measurements, or scope observations cannot be collected or conflict with the source request.
exception_paths.action: Keep the package out of quote-readiness review, name the missing or conflicting items, and assign requester clarification, a return visit, or owner review.

exception_paths.condition: The requester disputes a material scope note, measurement, exclusion, or recorded access condition.
exception_paths.action: Preserve both versions and the dispute, invalidate dependent completion claims, and require an attributable correction or owner-manager decision before review.
